data.reasoning: The package is a standard Python AUR package sourced from PyPI with pinned SHA256 checksums. The PKGBUILD uses standard build tools (python -m build, python -m installer) and applies two local, checksummed patches. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all 5 files, including the regex patch which the qwen model failed to process due to an API error. The regex patch is a benign code hygiene fix (adding an 'r' prefix to a regex string). No malicious injections, unexpected network activity, or suspicious build-time executions were found.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is entirely due to a tool error. The qwen model encountered an HTTP 400 BadRequestError when attempting to audit adafruit-ampy-regex.patch, forcing an 'inconclusive' verdict. The deepseek model successfully audited the same file and correctly identified it as a benign regex correction. There is no actual security disagreement between the models.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit adafruit-ampy-regex.patch due to an LLM API error (HTTP 400)
learnings: When a model fails with a transient API error on a single file, the audit orchestrator should retry that specific file or fall back to another model, rather than propagating the tool error to the final package verdict.

If an escalation audit is triggered solely because a previous model crashed/errored on a file, and the escalation model successfully reviews that file without finding issues, the system should recognize the coverage gap is closed and not require further escalation.
